mon.story: Anthropic's updated filing says it has promised to pay $895.4 billion in compute commitments, $69.8 billion of it in the next 12 months, while its operating loss shrank to $1.3 billion in nine months. Seven companies in its supply chain (Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, TSMC, Broadcom, AMD, Micron) are putting $26 billion back in as shareholders. The piece lands the week trading starts (19 Nov), so it is written from the final price, which the make session reads from the filing on the day.

mon.fact: Yahoo Finance, 13 Nov 2026, from the updated filing: compute commitments of $895.4 billion, $69.8 billion of it due in the next 12 months; operating loss of $1.3 billion for the first nine months of 2026 against $5.2 billion a year earlier; revenue of $33.2 billion for the nine months; and $26 billion raised from Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, TSMC, Broadcom, AMD and Micron, who buy non-voting shares at the public offering price.

source.label: Yahoo Finance, Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO (updated 16 Nov 2026)

mon.from: A newsletter lead in your inbox (The Deep View, 10 Nov), checked against Visa's figures as reported by The Paypers.
mon.so_what: Visa tested 22 AI shopping agents and found more than half of their failed runs still ended in a purchase: before you let an agent buy for your business, set who pays when it buys the wrong thing, in the contract and on the card.
mon.story: Visa's Agentic Commerce Benchmark put 22 AI models from 12 labs through 15 shopping tasks, such as buying a TV or a laptop. They passed 57.2% of runs, the best 82.2% and the worst 28.9%, and about 54% of the failed runs still ended in a purchase. The pricier models passed more often. The money question: when an agent buys the wrong thing, is it the shopper, the shop, the agent's maker or the card network that pays? Visa runs a card network and wants agent payments to grow, so its test is also its pitch. It differs from Wednesday's United option: that one is about who takes a cut, this one is about who pays for the mistakes.
mon.why_now: The Paypers, 6 Nov 2026, reporting Visa's new benchmark for AI shopping agents.
mon.fact: The Paypers, 6 Nov 2026: 22 models from 12 labs, 15 shopping tasks, a 57.2% pass rate (best 82.2%, worst 28.9%); 54% of failed runs still ended in a purchase; only 34.2% of scenarios were passed on all three attempts; the five most expensive models averaged 67.1% against 50.2% for the five cheapest.

source.label: The Paypers, Visa benchmark tests how well AI agents handle shopping tasks (6 Nov 2026)

beats: You ask an AI to buy you a TV. Four times in ten it gets it wrong.

Who pays for the wrong TV: you, the shop, the AI company or the card?

Our call on who ends up carrying the refund.

story.hook: Your AI assistant is clever, but on its own it cannot see your files, your chats or your code.

chain: An AI on its own only knows what you paste in.

MCP gives every app one shared language.
A connector is one app speaking that language.
Plug a connector in and the AI can read and act in that app.
Two connectors can share one job: find the file, then post the summary.
Rival AI firms now use the same language, so one connector works across them.
